haiku-low.q1: The old engine charges customers and writes the ledger. The new engine computes invoices into the shadow store and never charges or writes the ledger.
haiku-low.q2: The new engine charges customers and writes the ledger. The old engine computes every invoice into the shadow store and never charges or writes the ledger.
haiku-low.q3: Seven consecutive counted days, each under 0.1 percent mismatch with at least 5,000 invoices, and no unresolved shadow-era mismatches. A billing-owner member makes the move.
haiku-low.q4: Automatic trigger: new-engine fault rate above 2 percent in a 10-minute window, in both or new_only only. Shadow faults never trigger rollback.
haiku-low.q5: Every rollback ends in old_only after reset. Then a person must move it to shadow, and it needs 21 counted days before new_only.
haiku-low.q6: After deadline D, about day 33 with default margin, because skipped usage events cannot be reprocessed before retention expires. Planned rollback then fails precheck.
haiku-low.q7: Workers act on the billing_mode flag only if its mode_epoch matches the latest record they read and within T (15 minutes). Otherwise they stop charging and queue. In-flight invoice handling at a mode change: NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q8: Evidence lives in the rollout record and audit log. Forward moves are one step by a billing-owner member, a compare-and-set on record version, refused while a rollback is open.
haiku-low.q9: The rate monitor measures new-engine fault rate: faults divided by charge attempts in a 10-minute window. When above 2 percent, it applies the fence at once, runs precheck, and pages on-call.
haiku-low.q10: Due charges stay queued and are never dropped. They are made only after cutover to old_only, when the old engine's normal charge run picks them up.
haiku-low.q11: Each charge's idempotency key from customer and period, and the ledger allows one charge per customer per period, backed by the provider key. Unknown outcomes are resolved by key before any retry.
haiku-low.q12: Billing stays fenced with the rollback open and progress recorded. On-call is paged, and the step is retried until on-call completes it or, for on-call starts, aborts at D.

sonnet.q1: The old engine charges and writes the ledger. The new engine computes into the shadow store and never charges or writes the ledger.
sonnet.q2: The new engine charges and writes the ledger. The old engine computes every invoice into the shadow store and never charges or writes the ledger.
sonnet.q3: The shadow gate must be passed: 7 consecutive counted days, each with mismatch rate below 0.1% and at least 5,000 invoices compared (per-day reading is a working assumption, D1). Shadow-era mismatches still unresolved block the move. A person in the billing-owner role makes the move as a one-step compare-and-set on the record's version. It is refused while a rollback is open or the record can't be read.
sonnet.q4: An automatic trigger: a new-engine failure rate above 2% over any 10-minute window (with the proposed low-volume fallback to 60 minutes). It applies only in `both` and `new_only`. In `shadow`, faults are recorded and never trigger rollback.
sonnet.q5: Every rollback ends in `old_only`, with gates, counters and sign-off reset. The rollout then restarts only through a person's move from `old_only` to `shadow`. It needs the shadow gate (7 counted days), then the both gate (14 counted days) plus fresh Finance sign-off before reaching `new_only`, at least 21 counted days in total.
sonnet.q6: It is possible until the old engine is retired on day 35 after entry into `new_only` (if no rollback is open). Before then, a planned rollback from `new_only` must pass the precheck. The reprocess deadline D is the earlier of the oldest skipped event's retention expiry minus M, and entry plus 35 days minus M (about day 33 with M = 2). After D no planned rollback passes the precheck, because skipped events can no longer be reprocessed within retention.
sonnet.q7: Workers read the `billing_mode` flag, a copy of the rollout record that carries the mode, fence state and `mode_epoch`. A worker acts only if the flag's epoch matches the latest record it read and the read is within T (15 min default). The controller re-copies stale flags. NOT STATED: what happens to an invoice being processed at the instant of a mode change. The document only says the fence waits for in-flight charges, and unknown outcomes are resolved by idempotency key.
sonnet.q8: In the rollout record, the authoritative store for counters, sign-off, fence and rollback progress. The nightly comparison result must be written to the record within 24 hours. The gate counter must reach its requirement (and Finance sign-off for both to new_only). Forward moves are compare-and-set on the record version and are refused during an open rollback.
sonnet.q9: The 'rate monitor' (named in section 5) detects it. It measures new-engine faults divided by charge attempts in a 10-minute window. NOT STATED: any other detail about the component. When the threshold is exceeded, the fence goes up at once and the precheck then runs. If the precheck fails, the rollout enters `d9_hold`. During a config outage it applies the fence via the D12 path and pages on-call.
sonnet.q10: They queue and are never dropped (R7). Neither engine charges from `both` or `new_only` until cutover. After cutover to `old_only`, the old engine's normal charge run picks them up, skipping periods that already have a ledger charge or an in-flight charge, and skipping held periods. From `shadow`, the old engine keeps charging throughout.
sonnet.q11: The idempotency key derived from customer and billing period. The ledger allows at most one charge per customer per period, backed by the provider's idempotency key. Unknown outcomes are resolved against the provider by key before any retry. The post-cutover charge run also skips periods with a ledger charge or an in-flight charge.
sonnet.q12: The rollback stays open and the fence stays up, so charges queue. Steps are idempotent and resumable, and progress is recorded in the rollout record. Failed or stalled steps are retried and on-call is paged. On-call completes the rollback, or aborts it if it was an on-call start (before cutover). At D, an on-call start aborts automatically and an automatic start enters `d9_hold`. A failed cutover compare-and-set changes nothing, so re-read the record and retry.
